channel.description: Latest articles from MediaToday Co Ltd (maltatoday.com.mt)

item.title: ADPD: Dignity and decent living conditions should not be treated as charity
item.description: The Green Party says social support should be viewed as a year-round commitment, and not a charity move limited to the Christmas period

item.title: CMD extends residential street-cleaning service to five more localities
item.description: Residents in Sliema and St Julian’s are already benefiting from the service, which will be rolled out to Żejtun, Mosta and Dingli early next year, bringing daily cleaning to 34 localities nationwide

item.title: PN, Labour trade accusations over claims on generic medicines
item.description: A war of words erupted between the two main parties after the Nationalist Party rejected allegations of wrongdoing by Opposition leader Alex Borg, with Labour accusing the PN of spreading dangerous misinformation on public health

item.title: Woman grievously injured in Marsaskala traffic collision
item.description: A 44-year-old woman from Żejtun was taken to Mater Dei Hospital after a collision between two vehicles in Triq Sant’ Antnin on Thursday morning

item.title: Gourmet Today festive issue out this Sunday
item.description: The winter edition of this high quality food magazine is distributed for free with the MaltaToday on Sunday

item.title: Three shootings, a cocaine bust and omerta in Gozo
item.description: A bitter fallout between two prominent Gozitan contractors has reportedly escalated into a series of shootings and is now being linked to a major cocaine bust

item.title: Debt by a thousand payments: What party accounts reveal about PL and PN
item.description: The Labour Party overspent in an election year, while the Nationalist Party continues to wrestle with structural debt. MaltaToday takes a look beyond the headline deficits in the 2024 party accounts filed with the Electoral Commission

item.title: Jason Micallef’s arrogance must be cut down to size
item.description: Jason Micallef tries to frame his actions as a defence of Labourites like him. In truth it’s just a stupid excuse to pour vitriol on inquisitive journalists whose job is to hold power to account

item.title: WATCH | Toni Abela: ‘If you’re not coming in good faith, you need not come at all’
item.description: A few days after taking office as the first-ever Standards Commissioner for the Judiciary, retired judge Toni Abela sits down with Matthew Farrugia to discuss his new job. Over coffee and mince pies, they also debate the transparency of court procedures and how the judiciary is viewed by society
